title: I am flabbergasted... 100% procedurally generated, with LLM inside NPC
author: zuliani19
selftext:
I am flabbergasted... 

I always wanted to try this out: "3D with pixel camera, RPG,  I am flabbergasted, 100% procedurally generated, LLM inside NPCs"

I have tried it before in unity (I sort of have programing background, I have a SaaS with clients and all....) but game dev was always too much for me.

Two 4hrs nights after putting the kids to bed I gave it a try with Claude... and WOW... It did it all: the map generation with biomes and elevation, procedural cities with already enough detail, connected my openAI key to it... Seriously, I am really impressed

comments.author: Veerus616
comments.body: Muito interessante, porém qual a proposta do jogo?

replies.author: zuliani19
replies.body:
não faço ideia hahah eu saí testando e cheguei aí

Mas eu gosto da ideia de um jogo 100% procedural, desde os mapas até a história, com NPCs que reagem de forma orgânica à sua relação com eles, etc...

Eu gostei tanto do resultado que to pensando em tentar fazer virar um jogo de verdade, foi bem divertido chegar até esse ponto aí

replies.author: jumpythegecko
replies.body: You're kinda building dnd the video game. Sounds cool

comments.author: alone_explorer_27272
comments.body: It would be interesting if they added real combat physics, instead of numbers, half-sword style, and it would become a great procedurally generated fantasy game.

comments.author: Schedir
comments.body: I tried this with local models. Didn't work well. Good job. But you always need to pay a bit API

replies.author: zuliani19
replies.body:
Yeah, I know... this is a pet project thought

If I would comercialize it I think I'd make it a bring your own key application... I wouldn't have the patience to host (another) server haha

I have no idea how to keep a local ley that wouldn't be stolen...

replies.author: Total-Trash8491
replies.body: You don't hook a local key, you build a server that respond to the mcp calls. Your mcp hooks to the apis

replies.author: zuliani19
replies.body: I know... the point is: if I made this into a game, keeping a server would suck hahah

replies.author: zuliani19
replies.body: the fact that I did all this effortlessly in \~8h shocked me a bit

replies.author: Saytron3030
replies.body:
Effortless for sure
But yeah I get it. Pretty cool once you start then you realize you can feed your dog chocolate and watch it vomit all over the floor pretty effortlessly too

What do you feed your dog to make it shake and roll over and read Shakespeare?

replies.author: artbyepsilon
replies.body: "you" didn't do this tho. Claude did it.

comments.author: Drunkendrakon6
comments.body: How? I'm building with my old unity assets and stuff and can't get anything like this wth

replies.author: zuliani19
replies.body: Fable 5.2 can use blender... It made some of the assets, and others are procedurally generated (the houses are created procedurally from their floor shape)

comments.author: Saytron3030
comments.body: The models can literally do anything we want including being slop factories. Making something good and worth playing is really hard

replies.author: zuliani19
replies.body:
I know... It's the same with software: anyone can do something that looks and actually feels nice (not even slop, real, good software). But that's the 80%. The last 20% (security, REALLY good UI/UX, performance at scale, etc..) is where the money lives...

Before AI could code, I worked in a robotics lab (computer vision for Kuka robots was my research), I made an MVP and got real clients for a B2B SaaS (that is now a real software that is part of my monthly income haha) and for fun dabbled with game dev.

Honestly, game dev was by far the hardest coding wise. That is why I got so impressed by what Claude could put together in just some hours...
